meta.note: Real places on the Moon and Mars a user can pick as a target: mission landing sites and candidate landing or base regions. Every coordinate was read in the cited source; none is from memory. A candidate region's point is a published centre or site point, not a boundary. targetId links a place to the curated target of data/targets.json whose 55.6 km window holds it.
meta.coordinateConvention: Latitude north positive; longitude east positive, -180 to 180. The source's own longitude is quoted in each note. Mars sources do not always say whether latitude is planetocentric or planetographic; at this scale the difference is under 0.4 degrees.

sites.name: Deuteronilus Mensae exploration zone (DBDM EZ)
sites.mission: NASA Human Landing Site / Exploration Zone workshop 2015
sites.source: Head, J. et al. (2015), 'Mars Human Science Exploration and Resource Utilization: The Dichotomy Boundary Deuteronilus Mensae Exploration Zone', First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars, abstract 1033 (LPI). Accessed 2026-11-15.
sites.quote: The Dichotomy Boundary Deuteronilus Mensae (DBDM) Exploration Zone (EZ) (39.11˚ N, 23.199˚ E)
sites.note: Centre of a 100 km radius exploration zone with radar-confirmed glacier ice. East-positive; latitude type not stated. A second proposal at the same workshop (Plaut, abstract 1044) gives only a box: 39-43 N, 20-24 E. The IAU centre of Deuteronilus Mensae as a whole is 45.11 N, 23.92 E (USGS Gazetteer Feature 1509). Golombek et al. 2021 judged Deuteronilus Mensae too rocky for Starship in available images. Longitude as the source gives it: source gives 23.199 E; no conversion needed.

sites.name: Mawrth Vallis (ExoMars candidate landing site)

sites.quote: 7.4.2. Mawrth Vallis (22.160°N, 342.050°E; −2 km MOLA)
sites.note: East-positive 0-360; latitude type not stated. Runner-up to Oxia Planum for ExoMars. This is the candidate landing area, not the valley centre: the IAU centre of Mawrth Vallis is 22.43 N, 343.03 E (USGS Gazetteer Feature 3763). MSL-era ellipse coordinates for Mawrth were not verified. Publisher link: https://doi.org/10.1089/ast.2016.1533 (blocks scripted access, opens in a browser). Longitude as the source gives it: source gives 342.05 E on a 0-360 east-positive scale; converted to -17.95.

sites.name: Artemis III candidate: Haworth
sites.source: LROC data portal, NAC_ROI_HAWORTH_LO1_P867S3363. LROC RDR product page; cite as Henriksen, M. R. et al. (2023), 'Optimized Illuminated Terrain Coverage of the Candidate Artemis III Landing Sites with LROC NAC Controlled Mosaics', European Lunar Symposium, pp. 134-135. NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University. Accessed 2026-11-15.
sites.quote: Site Name Haworth Center Lat -86.7 Center Lon 336.3
sites.note: One of the nine Artemis III candidate landing regions NASA announced on 28 October 2024 (https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-artemis-iii-moon-landing-regions/). NASA published no coordinates for the regions. The value here is the CENTRE OF THE LROC NAC MOSAIC made for the region, rounded by LROC to 0.1 deg (about 3 km in latitude), not an official region centre. Mosaic bounds: lat -87.39 to -86.11, lon -34.98 to -12.36. The IAU centre of Haworth crater itself is -87.45, -5.17 (USGS Gazetteer Feature 14502); so the mosaic centre is about 0.75 deg of latitude away from the crater centre. Longitude as the source gives it: source gives 336.3 E on a 0-360 east-positive scale; converted to -23.7.
